items.title: Free daily JSON feed of Shanghai government subsidy notices
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/ZhongGheart/china-policy-data Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50267494 Points: 4 # Comments: 0
items.content:
A free, machine-readable feed of Shanghai government grant, subsidy and policy notices, refreshed daily. Built for researchers, consultants and AI agents working on the China market.

Live feed: https://shituapp.com/dot/api/programs.json Landing page: https://shituapp.com/dot/en/api.html

~150 notices collected from nine official Shanghai sources — science & technology commission, commerce commission, human resources bureau, development & reform commission, IP office, transport commission and the municipal government portal.

Any agent or workflow with HTTP access can read the feed directly. Example prompt:

Fetch https://shituapp.com/dot/api/programs.json and list every program whose isOpen is true, sorted by deadline. For each, output title, deadline, daysLeft and the official URL.

The feed is plain JSON over HTTPS, so any agent or workflow tool with HTTP access can read it directly.

For MCP users: wrap the URL in a generic fetch / http tool — no scraper or browser needed. A machine-readable site summary is also published at https://shituapp.com/dot/llms.txt

Records include titleEn and summaryEn for currently open programmes when available, so agents can answer questions without translating the Chinese titles first. title and url remain the authoritative fields.

The hosted feed is regenerated every morning at ~08:10 China time. A GitHub Action in this repo pulls the latest copy into data/programs.json at 08:30 China time, so the snapshot here stays current.

The compilation (structure, metadata, relevance scores) is released under CC BY 4.0 . The underlying notices are public government information; the original Chinese notice at each url is authoritative.

Attribution appreciated: Source: Shanghai Subsidy Radar ( https://shituapp.com/dot/ ) .

No warranty of completeness or parsing accuracy. Confirm with the official Chinese notice before applying. Not legal, tax or investment advice.

items.title: Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years in prison in sex trafficking case
items.summary: The trio - two of whom were high-profile US real estate moguls - were found guilty using their social status to lure women to parties and then raping them.
items.content:
Three brothers - two of them wealthy real-estate moguls - were sentenced to 30 years each in prison for drugging and raping dozens of women over decades.

Tal Alexander, 40, and twins Oren and Alon Alexander, 39, were found guilty in March of using their wealth and social status to lure women to parties and luxury homes, where they sexually assaulted them.

"Your conduct was monstrous," said Judge Valerie Caproni before sentencing them. "Your crimes wreaked havoc on their lives."

On Tuesday morning, the court in New York heard from 12 victims, including one who did not testify during the trial.

One by one, they spoke of the psychological trauma they endured after the Alexander brothers raped them, and their desire for the shame they had felt to instead fall on the defendants.

Many asked the judge to impose the maximum sentence of life in prison for each brother.

Maya Miller told the court that after Tal Alexander raped her in 2014, she lost all sense of safety. "I carry a quiet funeral within me for the person I might've become if this never happened to me," she said.

Another victim, using the pseudoym Isa Brooks, said after being raped by Tal and Alon Alexander when she was 16, she lost the ability to trust herself.

"I had no idea the danger I was in till it was too late," she said.

Another woman said when she planned to come forward about being raped, Tal Alexander threatened her, saying he knew where her sister worked.

Prosecutor Elizabeth Espinosa said the brothers deserved the maximum punishment for their crimes, saying facts "paint a truly devastating picture".

"For years, they honed their methods of luring women with the promise of luxury," she said, adding that they were "completely unmoved by the path of suffering they left behind them."

During the women's speeches, the three Alexander brothers showed little emotion. They stared ahead or conferred with their lawyers, who said they advised their clients not to look at the victims so it couldn't be misconstrued.

Attorneys for the brothers pushed for sentences of 15 years, arguing that they had become devoted fathers whose families would suffer in their absence.

The three men all addressed the court, continuing to profess their innocence.

"We had a work-hard, play-hard mentality," Tal Alexander said, adding he saw how his behavior "hurt people's feelings".

But their statements did not assuage Caproni, who chastised them for refusing to admit their crimes.

"How can someone who never acknowledged the wrongs they did be rehabilitated?" she asked.

At the end of the hearing, she sentenced them each to 30 years in prison for certain crimes. She also sentenced each to 20 years in prison for additional crimes, but said the men would serve the sentences concurrently.

During the five-week trial, 11 women - several said they were minors at the time of the assaults - testified that the brothers gave them gifts and flew them places including Aspen and the Bahamas where they fed them drugs before raping them.

Prosecutors said the brothers' pattern of abusive behaviour began in high school, though the trial involved crimes starting in 2008.

They said the three slipped drugs into women's drinks, and "physically restrained and held down their victims during the rapes and sexual assaults and ignored screams and explicit requests to stop".

Lawyers for the brothers argued the sex was consensual and that they were womanisers, but not abusers.

Two of the brothers, Tal and Oren, became wealthy selling luxury properties in New York and Miami.

They worked for American real estate giant Douglas Elliman, with clients including Lindsay Lohan, Kim Kardashian and Kanye West. In 2022, they founded their own New York-based firm called Official. Alon worked at the family's private security firm, Kent Security.

As they heard their sentences, the brothers stared straight ahead.

items.title: Reviewers rarely talk about reliability. Owners bring it up twice as often
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.bettascore.ai/research/reliability-reviewers-vs-owners Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50266780 Points: 27 # Comments: 31
items.content:
Across these 14 categories: 7.8% of reviewer opinions vs 17.0% of owner opinions. Owners bring it up more in 13 of the 14; tennis ball machines are the exception, with only 91 owner opinions. 6,900 opinions from YouTube reviews and 3,567 from Reddit threads. Left out: video doorbells, smart thermostats, mechanical keyboards and 3D scanners, where reliability isn't a topic of its own (it's folded into a broader one such as "Connection, Reliability & Support") , and pickleball machines, which have no Reddit threads yet.

Reviewers and owners talk about apps, software and connectivity about equally often ( 8.2% vs 9.4% of opinions). They don't agree on them: 21% of reviewer opinions on apps are negative, compared with 71% of owner opinions.

BettaScore ranks products by what public reviews say about them. No brand pays to be listed or to rank higher, and our shopping links earn nothing.

Each ranking shows what owners and reviewers say about every model, reliability included, with the quotes behind each score.

items.title: Expanding our partnership with GSA to bring Claude to all levels of government
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.anthropic.com/news/expanding-partnership-gsa Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50266701 Points: 10 # Comments: 4
items.content:
We are expanding our partnership with the General Services Administration (GSA) through a new agreement that gives government partners a 40% discount on Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API. For the first time, the discount applies across every product surface, including when agencies buy from us directly today and through cloud providers in the coming months. The discount also extends to state, local, tribal and territorial governments.

We are also launching a dedicated program to help agencies implement and make the most of their Claude use. These programs are commonly leveraged by our private sector customers and we’re looking forward to bringing those best practices to our public sector partners in the coming weeks.

Approximately 500 US federal, state, and local government organizations now use Claude. Weekly Claude for Government active users are up about eightfold since February, and usage across federal civilian agencies has grown about 20-fold in a year. Those organizations run some of the most important systems in the country, usually on tight budgets and with long procurement cycles. This agreement is built to support that work, so they can apply Claude to hard problems without a large upfront commitment.

The discounts offered through the agreement are estimated to save the government $1 billion. Agencies are not bound by a minimum spend commitment and will be able to pay for the usage they consume.

Government agencies are using Claude to solve some of their most important challenges. Examples include managing backlogs, records and forms, and modernizing old code. Some of the ways agencies are using Claude include:

Agencies can use Claude for their most sensitive unclassified work. Claude for Government, which delivers Claude's coding and agentic work capabilities and provides near-feature parity with commercial offerings at a FedRAMP High authorization level, was made generally available on September 30.

Agencies building their own tools can use Claude through Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud’s Vertex AI. On Bedrock, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High, with select models authorized for DoD IL4 and IL5 workloads in AWS GovCloud. On Vertex AI, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High.

Claude Enterprise is in process for FedRAMP Moderate authorization through the FedRAMP 20x program, marking the next evolution of how we are bringing the same innovative technology available commercially to the government.

Government agencies can buy Claude at the OneGov discount through GSA's Multiple Award Schedule today. Whether your department or agency already uses Claude or is interested in using it, our Public Sector team will help discuss your options.

items.title: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
items.summary: The truce was originally planned for the stranded residents of Oleshky, and Russia and Ukraine say no breaches have been reported.
items.content:
A ceasefire that began with the aim of getting food and medicine to the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky has been extended across the wider southern region of Kherson, according to sources.

Several thousand residents are trapped in the city with no access to food, water and electricity. On one side is the Dnipro river, while Russian forces are on the other and all the roads out are too dangerous.

However, no breaches of the truce that began early on Tuesday have so far been reported.

US First Lady Melania Trump, who helped broker the ceasefire along with Pope Leo XIV, said on Tuesday that the area involved had been expanded to provide "safe passage" for humanitarian convoys.

That was later corroborated by the press secretary to Ukraine's public ombudsman, and by Oleksandr Tolokonnikov, deputy head of Kherson, who said Russian shelling had stopped both in Kherson city, which is in Ukrainian hands, and the wider region.

Under the deal, the ceasefire will be followed by deliveries of humanitarian aid to Oleshky and then evacuations, planned for Friday, for anyone wishing to leave.

An estimated 1,700 to 2,000 people remain in Oleshky itself and a few thousand more in surrounding areas.

Many residents have resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive, telling the BBC they are suffering extreme hunger and want to leave.

Both sides said the ceasefire was being observed. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said everything was proceeding "according to plan", and paid tribute to US mediation and in particular representatives of Melania Trump.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said if the ceasefire produced results, it could "pave the way for other steps in the peace process".

A key official in President Volodymyr Zelensky's parliamentary party, David Arakhamia, said it would continue until 22:59 Ukrainian time on Sunday 1 November, and described the truce as the "largest de-escalation since 2022".

Before the war Oleshky was home to 24,000 people, but it was seized by Russia during the first days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

No shops are open, and the city has had no electricity, gas or water since the Kakhovka Dam was blown up in 2023, flooding the area and killing many people in Oleshky itself.

Conditions have become so desperate that not only is getting supplies into the city extremely difficult, but escaping is too risky because the routes out of Oleshky have been mined and subject to drone attack.

One woman told the BBC she had stepped on a landmine and was currently in hospital where she had undergone two operations: "I don't know how long I will have to spend there," she said, worried about not being able to join the evacuation.

Pope Leo appealed earlier this month to Russia's President Vladimir Putin to allow food and medical aid into Oleshky as well as a safe evacuation, and urged his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky to co-operate with Moscow over a ceasefire.

Then the White House said last week that Melania Trump had secured a ceasefire.

On Tuesday, the US first lady said on X that the area covered by the ceasefire "has expanded beyond Oleshky, within the Kherson region, to provide safe passage for the humanitarian convoys".

The current truce is supposed to enable roads to be cleared of mines for supplies to get into the city possibly on Thursday, and for residents to have safe passage out in an evacuation planned for Friday.

Russia's defence ministry said units from the army's Dnepr group had been conducting "engineering reconnaissance" and clearing main access roads into the village of "explosive and booby-trap devices".

Many details on the evacuation plans are unclear, and residents are wary of trusting officials with their names and addresses. However, a local volunteer told the BBC that about 500 people had already expressed interest by Tuesday afternoon.

Vladimir Saldo, the Russian-installed head of occupied areas of Kherson, said temporary accommodation had been prepared in the region itself as well as Russian-annexed Crimea and across the Russian border in the Rostov, Krasnodar and Stavropol regions.

Saldo told Russian media that most Oleshky residents wanted to leave the city and stay in Russia, although his account has not been corroborated on the ground.

It is hard to make contact with people there as communication is patchy and many are reluctant to speak of the situation in fear of reprisals from the Russians.

Those residents or relatives who have spoken to the BBC have expressed fears that Russia may not allow them to return to Ukraine, or might examine their phones and online activity for signs of Ukrainian support, which could put them in danger.

Ukraine's military general staff urged people not to trust unverified reports or spread rumours about "the routes, time and place of the movement of people and humanitarian convoys".

White House says Melania Trump brokered truce for Ukraine city 'on brink of disaster'

Eating garden weeds to survive in Russian-occupied city cut off from food and water

To stay or risk the 'Road of Death' - Ukrainian civilians trapped in frontline city

Zelensky has warned that routes out of Oleshky that are demined by Russia will ensure that those civilians leaving Oleshky will "head towards Russia and stay there".

He said some residents would get to Ukrainian-controlled territory "one way or another", and that ideally anyone trapped would be able to reach their destination and evacuate to Ukraine.

One resident called Serhii, who fled Oleshky through minefields around three weeks ago, said he had eventually returned to Ukraine via Russia and Belarus. He called for a route across the River Dnipro that avoided Russian-occupied territory, saying "you simply cannot trust the Russian Federation".

However, bridges across the River Dnipro have been destroyed and sources say the riverbank is also mined and dangerous, so crossing into Ukrainian-controlled territory appears impossible.

Across the river, in Kherson city, no explosions have been heard and no drone-related injuries reported since 03:00 (01:00 GMT) on Tuesday and cars and pedestrians have been moving freely, according to local reports.

"Judging from the fact that more people are walking around, it feels a bit calmer," Galina Kyrychenko, a resident in the city, told public broadcaster Suspilne.

items.title: Serie A: il Cagliari spaventa la Roma, la risolvono Mora e Malen
items.summary: I giallorossi si impongono 4-2. Lariani in rimonta per 3-1
items.content:
Vittoria per 4-2 della Roma all'Olimpico contro il Cagliari.

Il Cagliari spaventa una Roma stanca, la risolvono nel finale i cambi di Gasperini, Mora e Malen partiti dalla panchina per esigenza di riposo. Il 4-2 finale, che consente ai giallorossi di non perdere contatto dalla vetta, e' frutto di sorpassi e contro sorpassi fino quasi allo scadere. Roma-Cagliari non è stata certo una partita per cuori deboli, un luna park di emozioni da entrambe le parti perché quando l'amarezza di uno stadio Olimpico ancora sold out sembrava dilagante, arriva la zampata della squadra di Gasperini, prima in svantaggio, poi capace di ribaltarla, ma anche di farsi riacciuffare a otto minuti dallo scadere da Maldini.

Ma a differenza della gara contro il Real Madrid, la reazione d'orgoglio arriva e con i cambi fatti dal tecnico nella ripresa. Prima Mora di testa e poi Malen stendono la squadra sarda. I giallorossi si sono complicati non poco la vita, dopo che già una volta erano stati capaci di riprendere la partita iniziata con l'handicap per il rigore di Nzola. A rimetterla in piedi i due giovani della 'cantera', entrambi figli di Roma: Lulli e Pisilli. Poi, quando il Cagliari ha preso il sopravvento nel secondo tempo e Maldini jr., subentrato, ha siglato un giusto pari, e' arrivato il doppio colpo dei fedelissimi di Gasp. E così al triplice fischio l'urlo di gioia è tutto giallorosso, con la testa che potrà andare ora al doppio impegno in trasferta (Udine e Manchester) prima di chiudere il primo tour de force della stagione in casa contro il Sassuolo. Anche per questo all'inizio cambia tanto Gasperini che deve fare anche a meno di Paulo Dybala (fermo ai box per una lesione al gemello del polpaccio destro), oltre che degli infortunati Koné e Svilar.

Tra le scelte dal primo minuto, davanti a Gollini agisce la linea difensiva a tre composta da Mancini, Ndicka e Koulierakis. Sulle corsie esterne spazio a Lulli e Molina, con Wesley che si accomoda in panchina. In mezzo al campo la coppia è formata da De Roon e Pisilli, mentre sulla trequarti la prima sorpresa con Cristante che sale al fianco di Soulé per supportare l'unica punta Castro e non Malen. Una scelta dettata dal calendario intasato di partite, mentre è tecnica la decisione di lasciare fuori Mora almeno dall'inizio. Nonostante i cambi, il gioco della Roma non si snatura e riesce a recuperare lo svantaggio iniziale arrivato su calcio di rigore. Feliciani ha bisogno del Var per vedere il tocco di mani di Pisilli e assegnare il penalty alla squadra sarda che dopo 9 minuti è in vantaggio con Nzola.

La reazione giallorossa è però immediata e arriva dai giovani lanciati da Gasperini. E allora prima Lulli di testa e poi Pisilli ribaltano la gara; all'intervallo si va sul 2-1. E se per il 77 giallorosso è il secondo gol in stagione, e' ancora lui a mettersi in mostra con l'assist per il gol del sorpasso di Pisilli. Nella ripresa, poi, subito dentro Wesley per Molina, con i giallorossi in gestione ma il Cagliari spesso pericoloso, e la Roma a rincorrere il palleggio di prima della squadra di Pisacane, pericolosa con le accelerazioni di Fadera e Nzola; fin quando Maldini a otto dalla fine gela lo stadio con il gol del 2-2. Eppure la gara non finisce lì: come nel primo tempo anche nel secondo la reazione è immediata con il 3-2 di Mora di testa e poi il tapin di Malen che regalano alla Roma una vittoria più sofferta del previsto.

items.title: Israele spaccato: Netanyahu regge, ma il blocco di Eisenkot è avanti
items.summary: Il Likud primo ma non c'è maggioranza, volano i partiti arabi. Affluenza record
items.content:
A urne chiuse, nessuna maggioranza è emersa dal voto in Israele. Secondo gli exit poll di Channel 12, il Likud di Benjamin Netanyahu è in testa con 24 seggi, mentre Yashar di Gadi Eisenkot si ferma a 22. Tuttavia, il Change bloc dell'ex capo dell'Idf con 52 seggi supera quello del premier uscente che si attesta a 50. Un risultato storico e inequivocabile è stato raggiunto dai partiti arabi, con la Lista Unita (raggruppamento di tre fazioni) che ha guadagnato 11 seggi e Ra'am di Mansour Abbas altri 7.

"I risultati preliminari indicano una totale sfiducia nei confronti di Netanyahu e del governo del 7 ottobre. Se questi saranno i risultati definitivi, agirò immediatamente per sostituire il governo Netanyahu", ha dichiarato Eisenkot nel suo primo commento. In questo 27 ottobre, come in un gesto catartico collettivo, gli elettori si sono riversati in massa nei seggi fin dalla mattina alle sette per scegliere il futuro di Israele. Lunghe file, alluvione al sud, strade chiuse per il maltempo, tempesta di fulmini in centro, forte pioggia a Gerusalemme non hanno frenato l'urgenza degli israeliani di voltare pagina. Tutta la speranza di uscire da un incubo che va avanti da tre anni, affidato a una piccola scheda imbucata in una scatola di cartone azzurro. Come in una magia.

Fin dai primi dati sull'affluenza, pubblicati dalla Commissione elettorale centrale dopo due ore dall'apertura delle urne, è emersa l'imponente partecipazione al voto. Con rilevazioni che ogni due ore hanno segnato il superamento del dato del 1981, del 1977, e del 1973, anno in cui la Commissione ha iniziato a registrare i dati. Altissima la presenza alle urne degli arabi-israeliani, che rappresentano il 18% dell'elettorato del Paese, con le comunità beduine del Negev che hanno fatto registrare una partecipazione più alta che in diverse altre cittadine a maggioranza ebraica o ultraortodossa. Sui social e in tv centinaia di filmati hanno mostrato file di donne con l'hijab nero con la scheda in mano, pronte a votare. Un'immagine inusuale, anzi assente nel resto del Medio Oriente. Dove, su 319 milioni di abitanti dei Paesi arabi, gli unici ad avere regolare diritto di voto sono gli arabo-israeliani.

Netanyahu ha affrontato la giornata campale nondando i social con una valanga di post. Tirando fuori dal cassetto una strategia già utilizzata nelle elezioni del 2022, il premier uscente ha lanciato l'allarme: "Stanno cercando di rubarci le elezioni" . "Affluenza alle urne superiore alla norma nelle roccaforti della sinistra. Si tratta di una scelta tra la destra e la Palestina. Elettori di destra, è un'emergenza! Andate subito a votare per il Likud!'. In pressing sull'elettorato ha citato l'arresto di tre membri del partito arabo Ra'am che avevano buste con contanti per influenzare il voto. Poi ha pubblicato un video: "Siete avvertiti: l'affluenza tra gli elettori arabi al Sud è enormemente più alta di quella degli ebrei, dovete andare a votare! Portare la nonna, la zia, il vicino, niente mare o barbecue oggi" .

I toni drammatici di Bibi, da veterano avvezzo alle sceneggiature della politica, quasi stridono in confronto alla misura dell'avversario. Eisenkot, ex capo dell'esercito , un carisma pari a zero, a suo agio lontano dai riflettori, prima di recarsi alle urne ha scelto di far visita al kibbutz di Nir Oz, dove il 7 ottobre 2023 i terroristi di Gaza hanno ucciso 47 persone e preso in ostaggio altre 76. Ad accompagnarlo c'era Gadi Mozes, un agricoltore del kibbutz che fu trascinato da Hamas nella Striscia e venne rilasciato dopo 482 giorni di cattività. "Mi impegno a fare tutto il possibile per garantire di essere degni del prezzo che avete pagato", ha detto Eisenkot.

Poi, prima di votare, ha raggiunto il cimitero militare di Herzliya, dove è sepolto il figlio Gal, ucciso in guerra a Gaza. La Commissione elettorale si è riunita brevemente intorno alle 19 per rispondere alla petizione del Likud che chiedeva un prolungamento dell'orario di voto. La richiesta è stata respinta. Martedì i bar di Tel Aviv, quelli che di solito chiudono i battenti alle 18, sono rimasti aperti fino a notte fonda. Abbracciando le parole del presidente Herzog: "Le elezioni sono una vera festa per la democrazia".

items.title: One year of Dioxus fullstack in production: the good, the painful
items.summary: Article URL: https://oxidt.com/blog/one-year-of-dioxus-fullstack-in-production-the-good-the-painful Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50265960 Points: 18 # Comments: 10
items.content:
After a year of Dioxus fullstack in production, the Rust code is the most boring part of my business. CI is the most exciting part, and not in a good way: a release build takes 90 minutes on a GitHub-hosted runner.

That year started at my previous job and continued on my own products. Back in April I wrote about why I picked Rust for a production micro SaaS . The short version: slower at the start, cheaper to live with later. This post is the bill.

SeggWat is an in-app feedback tool for SaaS products. Its dashboard is a Dioxus 0.7 fullstack app inside a Cargo workspace: a backend crate with server functions, an auth crate, and about ten UI crates covering insights, feedback, ideas, boards, widgets and settings. Twelve crates depend on dioxus . Everything sits on PostgreSQL.

“Fullstack” means one Rust codebase doing three jobs. It renders on the server, runs server functions as the backend, and compiles the client to WebAssembly so the page becomes interactive.

Database query, business rule, server function, button: all Rust. One toolchain, one formatter, one set of habits, one place to look when something breaks.

That sounds minor until you’re a solo founder juggling several products. I don’t have a “frontend brain” and a “backend brain” that each need warming up. I open the workspace and keep going.

A struct gets defined once. The database layer returns it, the server function sends it, and the component renders it. When I rename a field, cargo check gives me a list of every place that broke, including the UI. There’s no OpenAPI spec to regenerate and no TypeScript interface drifting out of sync with the backend.

The win isn’t writing code faster. It’s refactoring without fear, late at night, with nobody to review it.

Dioxus can target desktop and mobile, including iOS, from the same component model. None of my products needs a native app today. But knowing I could ship one without a rewrite mattered when I decided where to put a year of work.

That’s the whole point. Once it compiles, it mostly just runs. A whole class of “undefined is not a function” bugs never reaches users, so the bugs that do get through are logic bugs. That’s where I’d rather spend my attention anyway.

The “boring in production” argument from April survived contact with real users.

The dashboard compiles twice: once for the server and once to wasm32 for the browser. A dozen Dioxus crates plus a macro-heavy UI add up. Locally it’s tolerable on a decent machine. CI is a different story, and the comments in my workflow files read like a diary of it:

At some point I stopped building images on every push to main. They now build on release tags or when I trigger them by hand, because 90 billed minutes per push is a silly way to spend money.

Every one of these helped. None of them changed the underlying math: two compile targets, a big dependency tree and lots of macros means a lot of compiling.

SeggWat’s insights page shows charts, and I couldn’t find a Rust charting library I’d trust in production. So the charts are Chart.js , loaded from a CDN and wrapped in about 340 lines of JavaScript that Dioxus calls through dioxus-use-js . Styling is Tailwind, so CI also installs Bun and runs the Tailwind CLI before Rust even starts.

I’m fine with that. It’s pragmatic. But if you’re choosing Dioxus specifically to escape JavaScript, know what you’re signing up for: Rust, plus some JS glue, plus a JS toolchain in your pipeline.

People ask, “What helps me ship fastest?” The better question is, “What helps me keep shipping without hating my life?”

For the backend, the answer is still Rust, and it isn’t close.

For the frontend, I’ve changed my mind a bit. If I were building something truly app-like, with heavy client state, offline support or a real mobile app, I’d pick Dioxus again. But most of what I build is dashboards: forms, tables, a few charts and some toggles. For that, I’m paying a 22-minute WASM tax on every release for interactivity I barely use.

So my next project is going to use Topcoat , a new fullstack framework from the tokio-rs org, announced in July .

It makes the opposite bet from Dioxus. Everything renders on the server, and components are async functions that can query the database directly. For interactivity, you write $(...) expressions in ordinary, type-checked Rust. Topcoat evaluates them on the server for the first render and also translates them to JavaScript, so they re-run instantly in the browser. There’s no WASM bundle and no second compile target.

On paper, Topcoat keeps what I love about Dioxus (one language, shared types, no API layer) and removes the part that hurts most, the 22-minute WASM build.

To be clear, this is a bet, not a result. Topcoat’s README calls it early-stage and experimental, with breaking changes expected. I’m giving up the multi-platform option. And I haven’t measured a single build yet.

I’ll write the follow-up with real numbers: compile times, CI minutes, and whatever I end up missing from Dioxus. If my release build drops from 40 minutes to 10, you’ll hear about it. If it doesn’t, you’ll hear about that too.

I’m Hauke. I build SeggWat , Stepshots and infra.page in Rust and write about it on OXIDT .

items.title: Ucraina: Stubb e Store chiamano Putin. Meloni, 'l'Ue non vada in ordine sparso'
items.summary: Asse con Copenaghen. Per Roma l'E3 'è morto'. Bruxelles: 'Per ora formati diversi'
items.content:
Novanta minuti al telefono con lo Zar. Novanta minuti che potrebbero fare scoppiare del tutto il caso di chi, per l'Europa, andrà a sedersi al tavolo con Vladimir Putin. Da Helsinki, il presidente finlandese Alexander Stubb e il premier norvegese Jonas Gahr Store potrebbero aver dato una svolta, in che senso poi si vedrà, al percorso negoziale che si staglia davanti agli europei sull'Ucraina. La telefonata con Putin ha avuto una base diplomatica bilaterale. Tradotto: Stubb e Store hanno parlato ciascuno per i propri Paesi. E ha avuto anche una sua logica temporale, arrivando dopo i colloqui di Oslo. In più, subito dopo aver parlato con Putin, i due leader nordici hanno chiamato Volodymyr Zelensky per aggiornarlo.

Ma il loro passo non poteva passare inosservato anche a Bruxelles, dove sta ormai entrando nel vivo il dibattito sull'identikit del negoziatore o del team di negoziatori. La notizia del colloquio telefonico, confermata da Helsinki dopo una girandola di indiscrezioni, ha raccontato di una conversazione "franca e sostanziale" tra i due leader europei e Putin. Il mar Baltico - con la necessaria libertà di navigazione - e l'Ucraina sono stati i temi sul tavoli. E' stata, e non poteva essere altrimenti, una telefonata interlocutoria, nella quale ognuno ha mantenuto la proprio posizione. A cominciare da Putin, che ancora una volta ha sottolineato come a una pace si potrà arrivare solo tutelando gli interessi della Russia. "I leader di Norvegia e Finlandia non hanno apportato nulla di nuovo", ha tagliato corto il ministro degli Esteri russo Sergei Lavrov. La sponda di Mosca resta invece più che mai Donald Trump.

Secondo il New York Times il tycoon sta valutando di togliere le sanzioni al principale fondo d'investimento della Russia, il Russian Direct Investment Fund. Una mossa che non farà certo sorridere l'Ue e che fa seguito al già contestato patto sul diesel siglato da Trump e Putin. Gli effetti più dirompenti del colloquio tra i due leader nordici e Putin, tuttavia, si sono registrati all'interno dell'Ue. Prima la Danimarca, poi l'Italia si sono fatte sentire. Con un messaggio riassumibile così: su chi parla con Mosca è ora che ci sia chiarezza. La premier danese Mette Frederiksen - che con Stubb e Store condivide l'area geografica - ha mostrato tutto il suo "scetticismo" per un'iniziativa "non concordata". "Onestamente, non so cosa pensino di poter ottenere quei due paesi con questa mossa", è stato il fendente partito da Copenaghen. "Abbiamo avvertito i nostri alleati", hanno replicato i diretti interessati. A stretto giro anche l'Italia si è mossa. "Bisogna designare al più presto, e in modo condiviso, una o più personalità con un chiaro mandato a parlare a nome dell'Europa", che "non può continuare a muoversi in ordine sparso e in formati che mutano di settimana in settimana, pena la progressiva perdita di peso nel negoziato", è stato il messaggio recapitato da fonti di Palazzo Chigi. Con una postilla: per Meloni il formato E3 (composto da Germania, Francia e Gran Bretagna) è superato. O meglio, è considerato "morto" dalla premier. Gli E3 erano al tavolo ai colloqui di Miami. A loro, ad Oslo, si era aggiunta la Polonia. Per l'Italia questo format non dovrà più ripetersi.

E il messaggio è indirizzato innanzitutto a chi, da Bruxelles, sta governando i negoziati sull'Ucraina: il Consiglio europeo e la Commissione, che sembrano avere posizioni per ora divergenti da Roma. La geometria variabile nei team negoziali, a Ursula von der Leyen, al momento appare la soluzione più idonea. "I negoziati si svolgono in diversi formati, in luoghi diversi e a diversi livelli, coinvolgendo capi di Stato e di governo, ministri, alti diplomatici e funzionari. L'Ue è coinvolta. Non abbiamo altro da aggiungere in questa fase", sono le parole di un portavoce della Commissione. Sul terreno, nel frattempo, la furia della Russia non si ferma con nuovi raid che nella notte hanno colpito Kiev anche a ridosso del campus universitario, seminando vittime e danni ad edifici residenziali. E' scattata formalmente, invece, la tregua umanitaria nella martoriata città di Oleshky. I residenti saranno evacuati attraverso la Crimea è una missione ad hoc sarà inviata da Mosca. La tregua - che porta il sigillo di Melania Trump ma sulla quale si è mosso innanzitutto il Papa - terminerà alle 23 di domenica prossima.

items.title: Ex-wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president freed after collapse of attempted murder case
items.summary: Marry Mubaiwa had been held on remand for seven years after being charged in 2019 for her then husband's attempted murder.
items.content:
The former wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president has been freed from remand after seven years while on trial for his attempted murder.

Marry Mubaiwa was charged in 2019, after her then husband Gen Constantino Chiwenga accused her of trying to impede his medical treatment in South Africa.

Ordering her release, a magistrate said Mubaiwa had suffered mental, physical and financial prejudice during the trial, state-owned daily the Herald said.

The ruling was made after the state asked for the trial to be postponed by a month in order to engage witnesses.

Her lawyer described the ruling as a victory that had come too late, because her client's rights had been violated by the delay in the trial.

Speaking outside court in the capital Harare on Tuesday, the lawyer added that if the state moved for a new trial, they would deal with it when it happened.

Mubaiwa was accused of attempting to kill Chiwenga, while he was in hospital in Pretoria. The vice-president then went to China for four months of treatment.

According to the New Zimbabwe news website, Mubaiwa celebrated her release outside court, and said justice had been achieved and that she was proud of her lawyer.

In 2017, Chiwenga played a key role in overthrowing then President Robert Mugabe.

items.title: Brasile: Bolsonaro fugge in Florida, Trump pronto a dargli l'asilo
items.summary: Senza passaporto a piedi in Argentina, poi in jet con la famiglia in Usa
items.content:
Due giorni dopo la batosta elettorale Flavio Bolsonaro ha violato il divieto dei giudici di lasciare il Brasile, ed è fuggito in Florida, insieme alla moglie Fernanda e alle figlie, Luíza e Carolina. L'amministrazione Trump ha già fatto sapere che è disposta a concedergli l'asilo politico. Ad aspettarlo il fratello Eduardo, anche lui latitante, che vive tra Orlando e Miami, grazie alla green card rilasciata sempre dalla Casa Bianca. E' l'epilogo di una giornata febbrile in cui l'ex candidato alla presidenza ha fatto perdere ogni traccia di sé alimentando una sorta di giallo internazionale. Atterra nell'America del tycoon, dell'amico di famiglia, da ex leader, perdente, sotto inchiesta e politicamente screditato: mentre era in volo il suo partito lo ha mollato riconoscendo la vittoria di Lula, che oggi festeggia gli 81 anni presidente per la quarta volta. Un gesto che segna plasticamente la fine della stagione politica del bolsonarismo.

Già ieri si capiva come sarebbe andata a finire. Dopo la visita al padre Jair ai domiciliari, forse per un ultimo saluto, Flavio aveva reso noto che il giudice della Corte Suprema, Alexandre de Moraes gli aveva intimato di consegnare i suoi passaporti entro 24 ore e di non uscire dal Paese. Fuori dalla casa paterna di Brasilia, Flavio ha detto la sua ennesima bugia: "Non intendo lasciare il Brasile, questa misura è assolutamente ingiustificata", protestava. Ma stamattina, dai media argentini sono arrivate le prime indiscrezioni su un jet privato pronto per il decollo nell'aeroporto di Iguazu,. E fra i nomi dei passeggeri c'era quello di Flavio. Il governo amico di Milei ha smentito categoricamente: Bolsonaro non è entrato nel nostro Paese. Intanto la polizia brasiliana era già alle calcagna, verificando ogni valico di frontiera. Scadute le 24 ore il giudice ha annunciato l'annullamento dei suoi passaporti, ma ormai era tutto inutile.

I suoi familiari avevano appena riferito ai media brasiliani della fuga verso di States. Con ogni probabilità lui e la sua famiglia sono entrati clandestinamente, a piedi, in Argentina, un po' come fece nel 2025 l' ex deputata bolsonarista italo-brasiliana Carla Zambelli. Secondo la Cnn, la soffiata del volo di Iguazu con lui a bordo è stato un depistaggio: pare che sia partito da un'altra città argentina. Ma poco conta, ora che è scappato. Raggiunge il fratello Edoardo, anche lui in Usa dal febbraio 2025 per sottrarsi al mandato di arresto emesso sempre dallo stesso giudice Alexandre de Moraes, quando era ancora deputato. E' stato condannato in via definitiva a 4 anni e 2 mesi di reclusione perché riconosciuto colpevole del reato di aver utilizzato il suo ruolo per sollecitare sanzioni economiche da parte degli Stati Uniti contro il giudice che stava indagando e che poi condannò il padre Jair a 27 anni per il tentato golpe del 2023. Su Flavio non pende alcun mandato di arresto ma è nei guai giudiziari fino al collo. E non essendo stato eletto, la sua immunità finirà a febbraio. Al momento è indagato alla Corte suprema federale su due fronti. Nel caso Dark Horse è accusato di corruzione, riciclaggio di denaro ed evasione di valuta, nell'ambito dell'inchiesta sul finanziamento del film dedicato al padre Jair Bolsonaro. In esame ci sono fondi riconducibili all'ex banchiere Daniel Vorcaro, attualmente in carcere per una maxi frode, e fondi pubblici parlamentari. Poi è indagato anche nel caso Willer Tomaz: qui l'accusa è sospetto riciclaggio di denaro e presunte irregolarità finanziarie legate a società, piattaforme di scommesse.

items.title: La manovra che verrà: flat tax per i giovani. Sull'Irpef si tratta ancora
items.summary: Previsto un fondo di un miliardo per le pensioni anticipate. Meloni: 'Manteniamo gli impegni quadrando i conti'
items.content:
Al puzzle mancano ancora solo pochi pezzi. Quasi tutte le tessere "sono andate a punto", la trattativa con l'Europa è conclusa e il testo della manovra è pronta al varo . Nel difficile equilibrio tra le innumerevoli richieste piovute sul tavolo del governo e la coperta corta delle risorse, trovano posto un pacchetto di misure fiscali per dare risposte ai giovani, un fondo da 1 miliardo per il pensionamento anticipato, c on un probabile rinvio delle misure ad un secondo momento, la detassazione delle tredicesime ma per i redditi bassi e l'estensione dello stop al bollo auto ai van familiari. Il tassello che manca è però quello centrale, il taglio dell'Irpef. Accontentare il ceto medio è la priorità di Forza Italia, ma un pallino anche della presidente Giorgia Meloni e il Mef ha avuto mandato di trovare in ogni modo le coperture.

"Siamo in dirittura d'arrivo sulla legge di bilancio" con "l'obiettivo di fare quadrare i conti e mantenere gli impegni presi", afferma la premier che snocciola i capitoli della manovra: " i salari, la difesa del potere d'acquisto, attenzione al ceto medio e alle imprese che investono e assumono, l'attenzione che va dedicata al tema del costo dell'energia, la sanità, la famiglia, i giovani saranno un focus della legge di bilancio " Dopo giorni "molto intensi", di lavoro "a testa bassa", anche il ministro dell'Economia Giancarlo Giorgetti vede la meta. Nel pomeriggio i leader di maggioranza tornano a confrontarsi per un ultimo vertice a Palazzo Chigi.

La quinta manovra del governo Meloni, che parte da 23,5 miliardi approda domani in un Cdm, non ancora ufficialmente convocato ma previsto per le 15. "A me danno gli ingredienti, alcuni li prendo altri no, li misceliamo, li mettiamo in cottura", spiega il titolare del Mef indossando il cappello da cuoco: "In questo momento è dentro nel forno, e quando tiriamo fuori la torta domani vedremo se è venuta bene, se si può mangiare o no". Arriva a termine anche la trattativa con l'Ue sulla flessibilità per l'energia.

Dopo le risposte arrivate da Bruxelles nel week end, i negoziati sono proseguiti sulle misure "ammissibili". Qualche spiraglio arriva già in mattinata: "Con la Commissione europea abbiamo fatto progressi", fa sapere Giorgetti, che poi in serata annuncia: "I margini nell'ambito della flessibilità della Nec li abbiamo praticamente definiti, quindi siamo soddisfatti". Sarebbe stata chiusa anche la partita del contributo che verrà chiesto alle banche, ma a quanto pare senza condivisione - in una situazione che alcuni non esitano a definire "tesa".

"Abbiamo trovato un accordo fra di noi, ma con le banche...", dice Giorgetti. Le indiscrezioni di un possibile incontro in giornata tra governo e istituti, del resto, erano state già smentite dal presidente dell'Abi Antonio Patuelli ("l'incontro a me non risulta"). Mentre il numero uno di Intesa SanPaolo Carlo Messina lancia un nuovo appello: sulle tasse "ci deve essere il giusto equilibrio". Dal contributo da 5 miliardi al settore finanziario dovrebbero essere escluse le banche di prossimità, mentre si sarebbe trovato il modo per ampliare la platea. Nella coperta stretta delle risorse, appena 9 miliardi al netto degli oltre 14 di flessibilità per l'energia e la difesa , il ministro dell'Economia, subissato in queste settimane da "tantissime richieste", promette una manovra che fa "il possibile, non l'impossibile" e punta a dare risposte alle cose "più urgenti". La linea resta quella della serietà sui conti, finora "apprezzata da tutti gli osservatori", rivendica Giorgetti, fiducioso anche sul giudizio in arrivo il 13 novembre da S&P ("penso che il rating sarà confermato").

Molte le misure dedicate ai giovani, in questi giorni in piazza per manifestare il loro disagio: dalla mini-Irpef per gli under 30 alla flat tax per gli under 35 neoassunti. Avrebbero trovato posto anche alcune proposte di Noi Moderati, come il libretto previdenziale, i l congedo a 6 mesi e la cedolare secca al 5% sugli affitti lunghi con agevolazioni ulteriori per i giovani. Sul taglio dell'Irpef al ceto medio, ad un certo punto sfumato e poi tornato in pista, Forza Italia non perde le speranze, e punta ad arrivare almeno a 55mila euro. La Lega incassa invece il miliardo per il fondo per l'anticipo pensionistico e la flat tax per gli autonomi. Questa è dunque la "proposta" con cui il governo passa la palla al Parlamento, dove il testo potrebbe essere incardinato alla Camera già martedì. Sarà lì che potranno arrivare "idee migliorative" ed essere trovate "risorse" finora non trovate, dice Giorgetti. Che non nasconde la speranza che "la situazione possa offrire maggiori margini nelle prossime settimane".

items.title: Early progress on accelerating drug development with Claude
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.anthropic.com/research/early-progress-drug-development Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50265609 Points: 93 # Comments: 86
items.content:
Anthropic’s life sciences team is working to accelerate curing disease. Over the past several months, our scientists have engaged in deep research partnerships with six organizations developing new medicines: BigHat Biosciences , Bristol Myers Squibb , Divergence Labs , Enveda , Generate Biomedicines , and The Column Group . We've also begun drug discovery efforts of our own. In doing so, we've learned a lot about how Claude can support drug development, and how we’ll need to improve Claude further to realize AI's potential in medicine. We plan to scale this work up substantially from here .

There are many opportunities to speed up drug development, even beyond the most commonly discussed applications of AI, like proposing initial designs for new molecules. Developing a drug involves many varied tasks: doing early research to identify a target for a drug and the right type of drug to engage it, designing a molecule with the right properties, optimizing it to be manufactured reliably at scale, drafting the regulatory filings needed to run clinical trials, designing and administering those trials, and much more.

Our strategy to realize AI’s medical benefits is based on having AI increasingly involved in all of these tasks. There is no single problem to solve; the bottlenecks are distributed all throughout the drug development process. The best way to identify and work through these bottlenecks is to get deeply involved in real drug programs, across many different disease areas and stages of development.

So, over the past several months, we’ve partnered with six organizations to do so. We’ve also started drug discovery efforts of our own, including programs for rare childhood forms of muscular dystrophy, where Claude handles much of the scientific and operational work.

This work serves our goals in three ways. First, it lets us better understand the strengths and limitations of our models in relation to a much wider range of drug development tasks (we’ve already prioritized specific improvements to our models based on what we’ve learned so far). Second, these programs can serve as case studies for the wider life sciences community. If Claude is to significantly increase the rate of new cures, we need to work with many more biotechnology firms and integrate Claude more deeply into their development processes. Third, these projects should, if their positive trajectories continue, have direct impact themselves. We’re optimistic that some may result in effective new medicines for the diseases they target, including food allergies, rare childhood diseases, and several forms of cancer.

In this post, we provide an update on our progress with our partners, along with technical reports and preprints that describe our thought process, methods, and early results in more detail. We then briefly outline where our work is headed next.

Generate Biomedicines: modality engineering. Generate Biomedicines has been working on increasing the usefulness of a cancer treatment known as CAR T-cell therapy. This therapy has historically helped treat blood cell cancers; Generate aims to reengineer it so that it can treat solid tumor cancers too. To do this, they’re aiming to shorten one part of the therapy’s genetic instructions, which would create room for additional instructions suited to other kinds of cancer. Six Generate scientists used Claude Code to propose new designs for this part. One design was about 70% shorter than the standard version, and in lab tests it was more effective: it allowed immune cells to make roughly 10 times as many receptors (the proteins they use to spot cancer cells), it killed tumor cells more efficiently, and the immune cells remained active for longer. Read more , and see Generate’s technical report .

Divergence Labs: hit generation. Divergence Labs is working on a novel way to treat food allergies. Food allergies are set off by a reaction from a molecule called IgE, some of which is attached to our immune cells and some of which floats freely in our blood. Divergence Labs is developing drugs that would detach the IgE from our immune cells entirely, rather than solely neutralizing the IgE circulating in our blood, as standard medications do. This could provide a much more effective treatment, but it requires a precise design, with two “arms”: one that would bind tightly to IgE, and another that would help prise IgE from the immune cell. Claude converted Divergence Labs’ goals into a detailed design plan, and then, largely autonomously, generated roughly 35,000 antibody designs in about a month to be narrowed down and tested. In those early tests, Divergence found “hits” for both arms: three designs that could bind to IgE, and 20 that could dislodge it. Three of those 20 appeared to dislodge IgE more than the standard medication. Its next step is to build a drug that combines the two arms. Read more , and see Divergence’s technical report .

BigHat Biosciences: lead optimization. BigHat Biosciences pairs AI with an automated lab to improve potential drugs (or “leads”), which must bind their target tightly, remain stable through manufacturing and storage, and avoid clumping together (among other criteria). BigHat’s scientists and an Anthropic researcher worked with Claude to improve these three properties in two leads, both antibody fragments that could become parts of future drugs: one designed to target cancer cells, and one designed to keep a drug in the body longer. Claude, connected to BigHat’s lab data system, Reccy, proposed changes to each molecule, and BigHat’s lab made and tested about 1,010 variants in about 10 weeks. Partway through, the team suspected the standard heat-stability and clumping metrics were misleading. Claude and the researcher reanalyzed the raw data, then proposed different metrics and a protocol change to test them. BigHat’s scientists refined and ran it, and the main predictions held. Compared with the originals, the best versions bound more than 10x more tightly, the cancer-targeting lead stayed in solution 18°C higher, and the lead for longer-lasting drugs clumped more than 100x more slowly. Read more , and see BigHat’s technical report .

Enveda: manufacturing and filings. To conduct clinical trials, companies need records showing that each batch of a new drug has been made to strict quality standards, and to submit an application to regulators, among other requirements. At Enveda, manufacturing chemists spent up to 75% of their time on paperwork. To ease the load, Enveda built a system that connects all of its manufacturing documents to Claude, then lets Claude flag any possible issues. Over tests on 1,061 pages of documentation, Claude caught all 11 issues that human reviewers had spotted—and flagged seven they’d missed. In the process, this method reduced human review time by 89%, from over 25 hours to less than three. Separately, Claude wrote the first drafts of two important regulatory documents. One took four hours, compared to about three months by hand. For the other, Enveda’s standard human review process found one minor error. Read more , and see Enveda’s technical report .

The Column Group (TCG): company creation. Because drug discovery can be slow, expensive, and prone to failure, investors in biotechnology companies have favored safer, previously validated ideas over riskier new ones, even when the latter could help more patients. We’ve been working with TCG to see whether Claude can change this by cutting the time and cost of drug discovery so that investors can confidently support more ambitious ideas. Specifically, TCG is establishing Pleiades, a new company that will use Claude to run many more—and more complex—drug programs than is usual for a small team. This could be a model for how Claude can reduce both the scientific and the operational and administrative overhead required to run a biotechnology company. If this works, this model could be replicated across the industry and direct investment toward harder problems in medicine. Pleiades is currently developing new tools and workflows for Claude; its very first Claude skill, which helps Claude assess whether drug targets are worth pursuing, has been evaluated on 45 target-disease pairs. Read more .

More recently, we’ve also begun working with Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) to find and address bottlenecks in clinical trial planning. BMS is using Claude to assess plans of an early-stage drug in clinical trials, and to estimate the likelihood of those trials succeeding. Together, we plan to expand this work in 2027 to understand its potential for increasing the probability of success in early development.

Michael Pourdehnad, MD , Senior Vice President, Head of Early Clinical Development, Hematology, Oncology and Cell Therapy.

In addition to our work with these partners, we’ve begun to run some research programs ourselves. We’ve acquired Mithril Medicine, a one-person company that has been developing treatments for two rare forms of muscular dystrophy. Its founder, Cody Tranbarger, used Claude to organize contracts, logistics, and experiments with 11 external labs, and delegated many other aspects of Mithril’s operations to Claude. As a result, Mithril took a possible treatment for one form of muscular dystrophy from an idea to promising results in mice in less than 18 months. Now at Anthropic, Cody is continuing this research, and plans to start several new programs. If his drug candidates continue to hold up, we expect a drug to be ready to start clinical trials in humans as soon as late 2028. Read more and see our technical report .

items.title: Raspberry Pi Zero 3W and Pi 4 Model A spotted in device trees
items.summary: Article URL: https://bret.dk/raspberry-pi-zero-3-w-pi-4-model-a/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50265594 Points: 81 # Comments: 25
items.content:
Two new Raspberry Pi boards have quietly turned up in Raspberry Pi’s Linux kernel tree, and neither of them is quite what I’d have guessed. Device tree files for a Raspberry Pi Zero 3 W and a Raspberry Pi 4 Model A have landed ( Phoronix spotted it first ), and whilst there’s no official announcement just yet, device tree files tend to give away a surprising amount if you can decipher them and I gave it my best shot.

The Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W launched almost exactly five years ago (tomorrow, in fact), so a successor has been a loooooong time coming. If you want a refresher on where things stood back then, my Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W vs Zero W benchmarks piece covers the jump from the original pretty well.

The headline from the Zero 3 W device tree is the SoC. It’s the Broadcom BCM2711 , the same quad-core Cortex-A72 chip that powers the Raspberry Pi 4 , replacing the Zero 2 W’s quad-core 1GHz Cortex-A53 RP3A0. If you want an idea of the sort of gap we’re talking about, it’s worth having a look at how those two compare on sbc.compare . That’s a big step up in per-core performance, and if they can get anything close to Pi 4 clocks in that tiny footprint, it’ll be a hell of a lot of compute for a Zero. I do wonder how toasty it’s going to get though, as the BCM2711 isn’t exactly known for running cool, and there’s not a lot of board for the heat to spread into. The device tree doesn’t tell us anything about clock speeds, so we’ll have to wait and see whether it’s been dialled back.

There are a couple of more speculative bits too. The PCIe controller is enabled and there are lines named PCIE_PWR_EN and PCIE_DET_WAKE, and the camera side pulls in a 4-lane CSI configuration rather than the 2-lane one the Pi 4 Model B uses. It’s worth noting that both device trees share a lot of copy-and-paste DNA (the Zero 3 W even has a duplicated “PWR_GPIO” line name), so I wouldn’t read too much into either of those until we see an actual board. I’d love to see PCIe exposed on a Zero, but I’m not holding my breath.

The second surprise is a Raspberry Pi 4 Model A . We haven’t had a Model A since the Raspberry Pi 3 Model A+ back in 2018, and the formula has always been the same: take the Model B, strip out the bits most people can live without (RJ45, some USB ports etc), and knock a chunk off the price. The Pi 4 Model A looks to follow that recipe pretty closely, though the price comment may not quite hold. Let’s see!

The device tree doesn’t tell us anything about USB. On the Model B, the USB 3 ports made use of the PCIe bus, and the PCIe controller is enabled here too, so USB 3 is possible, but the 3 Model A+ only had a single USB-A port and I’d probably expect the same here.

Here’s a quick side-by-side of what the device trees tell us, with the Pi 4 Model B thrown in for good measure. Anything marked with an asterisk is my interpretation of the device tree rather than something it states outright.

Quite a lot, I’m afraid. Device trees don’t describe RAM, so there’s no word on memory configurations, and there’s nothing on pricing, clock speeds, connector types or a release date either.

Pricing is the big one for me. Memory costs haven’t exactly been kind lately (I covered the last round of increases alongside the 1GB Raspberry Pi 5 launch ), and a lower-cost Pi 4 variant makes a lot of sense in that context. The BCM2711 is a mature chip at this point, it’s well supported in software, and a cut-down board gives people who don’t need a Pi 5 something cheaper to reach for. The Zero 3 W is a tougher one to call though, as the Zero range has always lived and died by its price, and I can’t imagine the BCM2711 being as cheap to build around as the RP3A0.

On the whole, I like what I’m seeing here. The Zero 3 W looks like the upgrade a lot of people have been asking for since the Zero 2 W landed, and the 4 Model A feels like a sensible way of squeezing more life out of the Pi 4 platform at a time when components aren’t getting any cheaper. The external antenna support on the 4 Model A is a really nice touch if it makes it to the final board.

Saying that, everything above comes from device tree files rather than an official spec sheet, so mileage may vary when the real thing turns up. Kernel support landing ahead of launch is usually a good sign that it’s not far off, and you can bet I’ll be throwing both the Zero 3 W and the 4 Model A onto sbc.compare as soon as I can get one in my hands.

Which of the two are you more excited about? Do let me know in the comments!

Related posts: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W vs Zero W Benchmarks – Pi Zero Showdown – 1GB Raspberry Pi 5 Launched Alongside Price Increases

Bret has worked with Raspberry Pi computers for almost 10 years now and in that time he's benchmarked and tested over 30 Single Board computers. In his day job, he's a systems administrator for a large cloud computing provider.

items.title: Tifoso in coma, 8 arresti e confessa l'aggressore di 19 anni
items.summary: E' fratello di un pentito e non va in carcere. Restano critiche le condizioni del 34enne
items.content:
Sebbene le ultime informazioni in possesso della famiglia aprano uno spiraglio alla speranza facendo trapelare "un piccolissimo miglioramento", restano "gravissime nella stabilità" - come recita il bollettino medico - le condizioni di Mario Spedaliere, il 34enne tifoso del Portici vittima della violenza ultrà domenica al termine della partita tra Puteolana e Portici, valida per il campionato di Eccellenza di calcio. S

pedaliere, colpito alla testa con una mazza ferrata, è in stato di sedazione profonda nel reparto di Neurochirurgia all'ospedale Santa Maria delle Grazie di Pozzuoli e la sua sorte resta appesa a un filo. Nella notte, intanto, svolta nelle indagini: con l'accusa di rissa aggravata, polizia e carabinieri hanno arrestato in flagranza differita otto persone coinvolte nei tafferugli, cinque maggiorenni e tre minorenni. Tra di loro anche il 19enne che, con una mazza ferrata, ha sferrato il colpo a Spedaliere.

Il giovane ha confessato: deve rispondere anche di lesioni gravissime. Solo per lui, tuttavia, non si sono aperte le porte del carcere. Il ragazzo, fratello di un collaboratore di giustizia, soffre di una patologia che al momento lo rende incompatibile con la detenzione dietro le sbarre . L'operazione della scorsa notte è la prima applicazione di rilievo delle norme contenute nel decreto sicurezza del 23 ottobre scorso, che prevede la flagranza differita anche per i minori. All'individuazione del 19enne si è giunti grazie alle testimonianze rese dai tifosi del Portici e alle immagini dei sistemi di videosorveglianza.

Il giovane ha anche indicato il luogo dove dopo il raid ha nascosto il bastone adoperato per colpire il 34enne, che è stato trovato e sequestrato dai carabinieri. Tra gli arrestati c'è anche un tifoso del Portici, amico di Spedaliere. Chiede pene severe il padre del tifoso: "Se questi me li ritrovo in strada un'altra volta, siamo punto e a capo", afferma con amarezza. Per poi aggiungere: "Voglio giustizia". Mentre il sindaco di Pozzuoli, Gigi Manzoni, rivolge il suo pensiero al giovane che lotta tra la vita e la morte: "Il nostro pensiero e le nostre preghiere sono rivolte a Mario e alla sua famiglia che non meritava di vivere questo dolore. Sapere che a ridurlo in quello stato è un ragazzo di soli 19 anni ci addolora profondamente". Una condanna alla violenza "senza se e senza ma" giunge anche dal prefetto di Napoli Michele Di Bari.

items.title: Egypt court fines journalist Lina Attalah and orders news site's closure
items.summary: Amnesty International said the verdict against Attalah and independent outlet Mada Masr represented "a crushing blow to press freedom".
items.content:
The editor-in-chief of the independent Egyptian news outlet Mada Masr was detained for several hours after a court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website and ordered its closure, her lawyers say.

Mada Masr said Lina Attalah was released once it paid the fine of 3m Egyptian pounds ($53,500; £40,100) also handed down to her by the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court. It was the maximum possible penalty for the charge, which she had rejected.

Amnesty International said the verdict represented "a crushing blow to press freedom".

It comes only weeks after six journalists working for the independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh were charged with belonging to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.

Egypt is among the top jailers of journalists globally, with 25 currently behind bars, according to the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ).

President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi has overseen what human rights groups say is an unprecedented crackdown on dissent since he led the military's overthrow of his predecessor, Muslim Brotherhood leader Mohammed Morsi, in 2013.

Tens of thousands of people have been detained, mainly Brotherhood officials and supporters but also leading secular and liberal activists, media workers and academics.

Egyptian journalists from fact-checking website facing terrorism charges

AI 'SpongeBob' parody of problems in Egypt draws scrutiny of authorities

TV presenter among 12 sentenced to death in Egypt drugs case

The CPJ said Mada Masr, which was founded in 2013, was a vital source of critical reporting in Egypt and that it had long faced pressure from authorities over its journalism.

The site had repeatedly sought an operating licence from the Supreme Media Regulatory Council (SMRC) since a new media law was passed in 2018, but that its applications were either rejected or left unanswered, the media watchdog added.

Amnesty International said Lina Attalah had also faced "years of harassment and intimidation", including six criminal investigations over Mada Masr's reporting.

Last week, prosecutors summoned her for questioning over allegations of publishing "false news" and operating a website without a licence.

Mada Masr's lawyer said the investigation included a recent report that the website had published about a wave of protests in prisons across the country, as well as a letter from the SMRC regarding its legal status.

Attalah was released on bail and later referred to trial before the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court on the charge of operating a website without a licence.

During Tuesday's hearing, Judge Mohammed Mubarak ordered the courtroom to be cleared of everyone except Attalah, her eight-person defence team, and Hossam Bahgat, head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR), an independent human rights group.

Bahgat told AFP news agency that security personnel then filed in before the judge announced that the court was denying several procedural requests made by the defence and appointing its own lawyer for Attalah.

"In a move that astonished all those present, the judge recorded in the official court minutes that the court had appointed a lawyer from the Lawyers' Syndicate to represent the defence," he said. "Lina herself spoke up to object to this lawyer being appointed to represent her, which the judge refused to record in the court minutes.

"In an even more shocking turn, the judge proceeded to dictate motions on behalf of this lawyer - who had not uttered a single word - and entered them into the official record," he added.

The judge then announced the fine for Attalah and ordered Mada Masr's closure "amid shouts and protests from the defence", before she was detained, according to Bahgat.

On Tuesday evening, Mada Masr said it had paid the full fine to the court and that Attalah was released after several hours in custody.

"During the release procedures, Attalah learned of a one-year prison sentence issued against her in absentia in 2024, on charges of publishing false news and managing an unlicensed website," it added.

"Her lawyers took steps to challenge the ruling, with a hearing in a retrial of the case scheduled for 11 November."

Amnesty International warned that the court's verdict marked "a dark day for independent journalism" in Egypt and demanded that it be overturned.

"This draconian ruling is the culmination of years of relentless harassment and unjust proceedings designed to shut down one of the country's last remaining independent media voices," said the group's senior director for regional impact, Yasmine Ahmed.

"Lina Attalah should never have been prosecuted for exercising her right to freedom of expression and doing her journalistic job."

CPJ Regional Director Sara Qudah said: "If Egypt can put in custody one of its most respected editors and shut down her newsroom, no independent journalist in the country is safe. Attalah must be released immediately, and Mada Masr must be allowed to keep reporting."

items.title: Hex Raises $100M
items.summary: Article URL: https://hex.tech/blog/hex-new-era/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50265413 Points: 35 # Comments: 19
items.content:
Announcing Hex 4.0, and a $100m fundraise — building toward the agent-native future for analytics.

A few months ago, after we had just closed our best-ever quarter, we decided to do something bold: start from scratch on a clean-sheet version of Hex, the product we had been building for 6 years and used by over 2,500 customers globally.

This was a radical thing to do — but after 4 years on the frontier of bringing AI to data, we knew it was the right one. Today we’re introducing that new version — and announcing a fundraising to bring it to the world.

This was the question we asked ourselves earlier this year. See, we were founded in 2019, making us a pre-AI company (ew!).

Now, I also think we had done an amazing job bringing AI into our product over those years! We had a text-to-SQL prototype using GPT-3 before ChatGPT. We launched our Magic features in February 2023. We launched the first really good data agent last year, and earlier this year we changed the game again with generative apps . I'm proud of all of this.

But fundamentally, we were trying to integrate AI into a product that already existed. Our data model, architecture, and core assumptions around what users were doing in our product were all baked in 2020 to 2021 — we were far from “agent native”, no matter how much we liked saying it. ¹

And this was leading to some major issues: our agent harness was becoming bloated with hundreds of tools, which were required to teach agents about how to use Hex-something emphatically out of distribution. Our compatibility with external agents, because those products were having to use Hex through a keyhole via MCP versus being able to work with something more native. And our compute engine wasn’t built to support the high-speed, high-concurrency, iterative workflows agents seem to like.

In parallel with these issues, we were seeing data work is happening in a lot of other places : folks are using Cursor, Codex, Cognition, Claude, and custom agents — which in turns was causing a lot of issues! People are "vibe coding" dashboards and reports way more than they're using their legacy BI tools and emailing around HTML files without provenance, context, or permissions. It’s a mess — but the previous version of Hex couldn’t solve this in the way we wanted.

Altogether, this added to a growing sense that – despite growing quickly and having a lot of happy customers – we were headed for a point of diminishing returns.

As we got together and talked about this, we had an idea of what we actually would do if we were starting from scratch today: a platform rooted in code — with all of its infinite flexibility and agent nativity — and embrace that data work can happen a lot of places, but that it needs context, controls, guidance, and guardrails to make it trusted.

Hex 4.0 is truly a from-scratch rewrite for the era of agents (and, of course, was greatly accelerated by using agents to write all of the code, guided by the decades of combined expertise from our teams in building scaled data platforms).

The core assumption of 4.0 is that everything is code — and that teams need context, controls, and compounding to make it trusted and scalable. It leans into the idea that data work is happening in a lot of places, and that "plain code" (not a proprietary YAML format) is the way to make that make sense.

We have a big, long blog post detailing all of this here , I recommend you read it! Maybe a couple of times, because it's interesting, and we suspect you’re going to be hearing from a lot of other companies who are going to realize that they need to think from first principles too.

And this is just the foundation for a lot of other things we have in mind; in fact, one of the reasons we went so hard on this is because there are things we want to build we couldn't imagine doing on the old architecture — but are trivial on the new one.

As this all came into focus, we realized more money would help us go faster – to scale our team, expand go-to-market, and continue to make great swag. The only problem was that in the first part of the year, investors thought all software was going to die and there would only be two companies left. ²

Shailendra and the team at Peak XV, however, didn't think that: in fact, they were pretty sure that model-independent platforms were going to have a bright future ahead. And they were not scared about us taking a bold first-principles approach to go build it.

So I’m excited to announce that we’ve closed a $100 million financing round at a $1.2B valuation led by PeakXV and our 137 Ventures, with participation from Amplify, Avra, a16z, Redpoint, Sequoia, and Zero Prime.

This gives us a bunch more runway to keep building this thing, and take more bold bets into the future.

I'm throwing some serious shade at the "SaaS apocalypse"-pilled investors above, but I'll give them some credit: I think it is true that a lot of software categories will effectively die over the next couple of years. But I also believe many will combine and be reborn into new shapes.

This is our basic outlook on BI: the old paradigm is over, and no amount of bolting a chatbot sidebar onto the legacy platforms is going to change that. But there are also fantastic new opportunities opening up!

We believe the next chapter is rooted in code, with the context and controls needed to establish trust, governance, and guardrails.

The basic promise of BI is finally here: everyone can ask questions! Everyone can build! But now it's chaotic, and all the trust is gone. We see this as the core trade-off to break, and we're kind of obsessed with it.

¹ I'm not going to call out anyone by name, but I do think it's funny how many companies in our space that have been around for 8 years or more now call themselves "AI native", despite that literally being the antithesis of that phrase. I mean, I get why they're doing it, but unless you have literally rebuilt your product in the last 24 months, I'm not sure you can credibly claim it...

² I'm joking, but not really? You should have sat in some of the pitch meetings we had…

items.title: Camera, bocciata richiesta di Magi per la nascita nuovo gruppo: no della destra, centristi assenti
items.summary: Non è stata concessa la deroga per la formazione di +Europa, Centro democratico, Stati Uniti d’Europa. Magi: “L'ufficio di presidenza ha deciso di fare politica elettorale”
items.content:
L'ufficio di presidenza della Camera ha bocciato la richiesta per la nascita del nuovo gruppo +Europa, Centro democratico, Stati Uniti d'Europa. Non è stata concessa la deroga per la formazione del nuovo gruppo composto da cinque deputati: Riccardo Magi, Benedetto Della Vedova, Luca Pastorino, Bruno Tabacci e Aboubakar Soumahoro . La maggioranza ha votato contro la deroga, a favore le opposizioni. A quanto si riferisce, non erano presenti i rappresentanti di Iv, Azione e 1 deputato 5 Stelle.

“I requisiti per la costituzione del gruppo c'erano tutti ma l'ufficio di presidenza ha deciso di fare politica elettorale – dichiara il segretario di +Europa Riccardo Magi al termine dell'ufficio di presidenza della Camera – Così tanta paura hanno avuto della nascita di un piccolo gruppo che avrebbe potuto promuovere un ricorso alla Corte sul punto specifico delle firme e del sistema arbitrario e discriminatorio di esenzioni dalla raccolta che è stato approvato nella legge elettorale a sugellarne l'incostituzionalità. Ovvio che gli autori di tali privilegi e i diretti beneficiari si siano opposti alla nostra iniziativa dichiarata alla luce del sole. Ne hanno avuto paura quelli che in maggioranza ci hanno votato contro e quelli che dalle opposizioni hanno fatto mancare i voti a sostegno di un'altra forza di opposizione".

Continua Magi: "Determinante è stata anche la mancanza di sostegno da parte delle altre opposizioni che avrebbero potuto garantire il riconoscimento del gruppo favorendo l'ingresso in esso di un deputato in più. Il gruppo avrebbe anche favorito una convergenza tra le forze dell'area riformatrice del centro sinistra. Di certo non ci abbatteremo, siamo solo più consapevoli di cosa siano capaci gli avversari e i finti alleati", conclude il segreteario di +Europa.
